headline: One-time gain masks shrinking subscriber base

summary_short: EchoStar reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.58 billion (-4.0% y/y) and net income of $8.46 billion, though the profit reflects a $9.73 billion non-cash deconsolidation gain tied to Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation's Chapter 11 filing; excluding that, net income was about $49.5 million.
summary_long: Revenue fell 4.0% year-over-year to $3.58 billion, with declines concentrated in Pay-TV ($2.25B, -241,000 subscribers) and Broadband & Satellite Services ($316.9M, -59,000 subscribers); Wireless was roughly stable at $929M (-118,000 subscribers). Diluted EPS was $24.12 and net income $8.46 billion, both driven almost entirely by a ~$9.73 billion non-cash gain on deconsolidation following Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation's and several subsidiaries' Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing on August 2, 2026; excluding that gain, net income was approximately $49.5 million. Shareholders' equity fell to $14.16 billion from $19.74 billion a year earlier, and cash fell to $440.0 million. The release included no forward guidance or capital-return announcements.
confidence_notes: The event's resolved sourceLink (SEC 8-K accession 0001415404-26-000038) turned out to be a DIFFERENT same-day filing -- items 1.03/2.04/5.02/7.01/8.01/9.01 announcing subsidiary Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation's Chapter 11 bankruptcy petition -- not an earnings release; a resolver source-matching issue worth flagging upstream. A search for the actual Item 2.02 earnings 8-K on EDGAR's recent-filings list for this CIK did not surface one, so this summary is sourced from EchoStar's own IR press release (fetched via a GlobeNewswire mirror after the IR page itself timed out on fetch). The $8.46B net income / $24.12 diluted EPS are dominated by a ~$9.73B non-cash deconsolidation gain tied directly to the HSSC bankruptcy filing referenced above -- both events are the same underlying story. All KPI figures reconcile exactly between the resolver's SEC-XBRL shard data and the company's own release.

drivers.explanation: Decline was concentrated in Pay-TV ($2.25B vs $2.46B, -241,000 subscribers) and Broadband & Satellite Services ($316.9M vs $339.8M, -59,000 subscribers); Wireless was roughly stable (-118,000 subscribers, revenue flat).
Net income was primarily a non-cash ~$9.73 billion gain on deconsolidation tied to Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation's Chapter 11 filing; excluding it, net income was approximately $49.5 million.
